issues.current_text: A Huawei, rival chinesa, já detém mais de 50% do mercado local.
issues.previous_text: A consultoria TrendForce projeta que chips fabricados na China podem capturar metade do mercado doméstico de processadores avançados de IA ainda em 2026.
issues.suggestion: The Huawei 50%+ market share claim is essentially the same data point as May 1's TrendForce projection. Cut the Huawei sentence or reframe it as continuity: e.g., 'a Huawei, que como projetado já ultrapassou 50% do mercado local' — acknowledging the reader already knows this. Better yet, drop the percentage and focus on what's genuinely new: Jensen Huang's zero-share admission and 'counterproductive' quote.

issues.current_text: Huang chamou a política americana de 'já amplamente contraproducente' e alertou que abandonar um mercado do tamanho da China é estrategicamente insensato.
issues.previous_text: A Huawei espera que a receita com chips de IA atinja cerca de US$12 bilhões em 2026, 60% acima dos US$7,5 bilhões do ano anterior. [...] A consultoria TrendForce projeta que chips fabricados na China podem capturar metade do mercado doméstico.
issues.suggestion: Both editions frame the China chip story through the same lens: US export controls backfired, Chinese companies filled the gap. May 1 showed the Huawei/DeepSeek side; May 4 shows the Nvidia/Jensen side. The angle is complementary but the narrative arc ('export controls → China wins') is identical. Consider anchoring May 4 on what's different: Jensen's rare public admission and the political confrontation in Congress, rather than re-establishing the 'backfire' thesis the reader already absorbed.

issues.current_text: Anthropic appears 3 times: joint venture with Blackstone/Goldman ($1.5B), Claude Security beta, and MiMo comparison to Claude Opus 4.6
issues.previous_text: Anthropic appears 3 times: excluded from Pentagon as supply-chain risk, listed as Coatue/Next Frontier client, and Musk ranking Anthropic first among labs
issues.suggestion: Anthropic is mentioned 3 times in both consecutive editions. Each mention is a different story, so it's not a content repeat — but the cumulative effect is that the newsletter reads as Anthropic-centric. Consider dropping the MiMo-vs-Claude-Opus comparison (use a benchmark name or another frontier model as the reference point) to reduce Anthropic density to 2 mentions.

issues.current_text: A OpenAI anunciou iniciativa semelhante — a DeployCo, com US$4 bilhões comprometidos.
issues.previous_text: O Departamento de Defesa dos EUA formalizou os acordos com oito empresas — SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, Oracle e a startup Reflection AI — para implantar modelos de IA nos níveis mais altos de segurança das redes militares
issues.suggestion: OpenAI's enterprise/government deployment push appeared in May 1 (Pentagon GenAI.mil) and now in May 4 (DeployCo). The DeployCo mention is brief and serves as context for the Anthropic JV, which is fine — but flag it as a pattern. If OpenAI enterprise deployment stories keep appearing, they need to be threaded as a running narrative rather than treated as standalone each time.

summary: Moderate repetition: the Huawei/China market share data point is nearly duplicated, and the 'export controls backfired' framing carries over unchanged from May 1. Anthropic's 3-mention density in back-to-back editions risks monotony. No repeated phrasing at the sentence level.
